Image of His Son. They will indeed be raised, all bodies, by the grace of incorruptibility, those humiliated, but they will not all be changed. But the wicked remain in the form of dishonor, needing only to be punished, and the righteous are changed only to the good of incorruptibility, and having enriched the halo. He therefore, by His own power and godly energy, will transform the body of our humiliation to be like the body of His glory. But what is the body of our humiliation? This is the earthly, the humiliated by death from that ancient earth, which Christ, becoming a curse for us, loosed. The transformation will not bring us to another nature, for we will be what we are, that is, men, but more excellent, incomparably. For we will be incorruptible and imperishable, and moreover glorified. What then would the last trumpet, which stirs the dead, want to show us, He the pious Paul explains, saying, 'For the Lord Himself, in a command, in the voice of an angel'

pass_b_english: They will indeed be raised, all bodies, by the grace of incorruptibility, but they will not all be changed.
The wicked will remain in the form of dishonor, needing only to be punished, while the righteous will be changed to the good of incorruptibility and will have enriched their surrounding light.
He, by His own power and godly energy, will transform the body of our humiliation to be like the body of His glory.
The body of our humiliation is the earthly body, humiliated by death from that ancient curse, which Christ, becoming a curse for us, loosed (Galatians 3:13).

This transformation will not bring us to another nature, for we will be what we are, that is, human beings, but more excellent, incomparably, for we will be incorruptible and imperishable, and moreover glorified.
The last trumpet, which stirs the dead, is mentioned by the apostle Paul, who says that the Lord Himself, in a command, in the voice of an archangel (1 Thessalonians 4:16).
